extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent attorneys/applicants (Korean Intellectual Property Office context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for determining unity of invention among patent claims (including special cases) and procedural/substantive requirements for deposit of microorganisms in patent applications filed in Korea. Covers criteria, examples, and examination instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of inventions — common special technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims include the special technical features of other claims: if a claim's special technical feature is the common special technical feature among claims, unity of inventions is met among those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1: Lamp filament A; Claim 2: Lamp B comprising Lamp filament A; Claim 3: Searchlight comprising Lamp B comprising Lamp filament A and Spinning rim C. If Filament A in claim 1 is the special technical feature common to all claims, unity is met among claims 1, 2 and 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity when claims disclose corresponding special technical features (sub-combination and sub-combination)
rubrics_metrics.description: If different claims disclose special technical features that correspond to each other (e.g., complementary sub-combinations), unity of inventions is met between those claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1: transmitter comprising timebase expander; Claim 2: receiver comprising timebase compressor. If the expander and compressor are corresponding special technical features (sub-combination and sub-combination), unity is met among claims 1 and 2. Claim 3 including all features of claims 1 and 2 meets unity with each as well (combination and sub-combination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity not met when claims recite non-identical/non-corresponding special technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the special technical features are not identical or do not correspond, unity of inventions is not met between claims that recite different special technical features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1: DC motor control circuit A; Claim 2: DC motor control circuit B; Claim 3: apparatus using motor comprising control circuit A; Claim 4: apparatus using motor comprising control circuit B. Unity is met between claim 1 and claim 3, or claim 2 and claim 4, but not between claim 1 and claim 2 or claim 3 and claim 4, because control circuit A and B are different special technical features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity with claims reciting multiple features (non-single features)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims recite distinct features (e.g., Feature A and Feature B), unity is met between claims that share one of those features and a claim combining them, but not between claims each having only different single features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1: conveyor belt comprising Feature A; Claim 2: conveyor belt comprising Feature B; Claim 3: conveyor belt comprising Features A and B. Unity is met between claim 1 and claim 3, and between claim 2 and claim 3, but not between claim 1 and claim 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and manufacturing method — 'suitable' criterion for unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between a product invention and a manufacturing method invention is determined based on whether the manufacturing method is 'suitable' for the manufacture of the concerned product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Suitable' indicates that when the manufacturing method is practiced, the product is manufactured. 'Suitable' does not necessarily mean the product cannot be manufactured by other methods or that the manufacturing method cannot be used for other products. Examples provided (chemical material X and its manufacturing method; corrugated cardboard and manufacturing steps; golf ball manufactured by specified method) illustrate suitability and common special technical feature identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturing method must be a method of manufacturing the product itself (indirect/secondary methods excluded)
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacturing method must be a method of manufacturing the concerned product in itself. Methods used indirectly or secondarily for manufacturing the product (for example, methods of analysis) shall not be filed as one application unless special conditions exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance warns examiners/applicants that analytical or indirect methods are not considered manufacturing methods for unity grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and method of using the product — correspondence by using quality/functions
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention of a method of using a product corresponds to the product invention when the method uses the quality or functions of the concerned product; the method of using is deemed to correspond to the product when it relates to using a product's special qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1: Material A; Claim 2: method of deinsectization with Material A — Claim 2 corresponds to a method of using the insecticidal property of Material A. Another example explains a manufacturing method phrased as production but substantively a method of using Material A to suppress fungus in soy sauce, thus corresponding to the product's special qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and method of treating the product — definition and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Treating the product' means applying an external effect to maintain or exert the product's functions without changing the product's nature. Such treating methods correspond to the product invention for unity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Claim 1: prefabricated home with special structure; Claim 2: method of storing such home — storing intends to maintain/exert the function (easily-stored/transferred), so it corresponds. Another example: material A and method of storing material A by specific conditions — corresponds to treating the subject matter in claim 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product and machinery/device for manufacturing the product — suitability and unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether equipment used for manufacturing a product is suitable for manufacturing the product shall be crucial; if the equipment, when practiced, actually manufactures the product, unity is met between the product claim and the equipment claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Suitable' again means that practicing the equipment invention results in manufacture of the product, even if equipment can be used for other products. Example: Bolt A with special structure and Equipment B used for manufacturing Bolt A — unity met. The guidance reiterates suitability does not require exclusivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment must be a device directly used for manufacturing; indirect devices excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment refers to a device that can be used for manufacturing the product in itself. Devices that are indirectly or secondarily used for manufacturing the product (for example, measuring or analytical devices) cannot be filed as one application as equipment for the product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should exclude measuring/analytical devices from the same application as the manufacturing product unless they are directly part of manufacturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Other products' includes chemical materials or microorganisms (for unity)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Other products' shall include chemical materials or microorganisms besides equipment; such other products that correspond to manufacturing of the product can meet unity of inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Claim 1: Antibiotic A; Claim 2: New culture B manufacturing Antibiotic A — culture B corresponds to 'other products' manufacturing antibiotics; unity is met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method and machinery/equipment directly used for practicing the method — 'suitable' determined by direct use for manifestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where machinery, equipment, or other products are directly used for practicing the method, unity is met. 'Suitable' is determined based on whether those items are directly used for manifestation of the special technical features of the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Microorganism X that plays a manufacturing role can be considered 'other products' used for manufacturing antibiotic A. A paint comprising rust resistant material X corresponds to a product directly used for practicing a painting method with special electrode placement and current load.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush-type claims — corresponding alternatives yield unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Where alternative elements are recited in the Markush style in a single claim, if the alternative elements have corresponding qualities or functions, unity of inventions is met. The same criteria apply whether alternatives are in multiple independent claims or in a single Markush claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Markush group includes alternative chemicals that meet other chapter requirements, the group is considered to have corresponding qualities/functions. Example: a formula where indole is the crucial structural element common among substituents; all claimed compounds deemed to have same use so unity is met. Another example: catalysts (X) and (X+a) share common element and activation and thus meet unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group with at least one alternative lacking novelty requires unity review
rubrics_metrics.description: If at least one alternative element among the alternatives in a Markush group is determined to lack novelty over prior art, an examiner shall review unity of inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must reassess unity when variants in a Markush grouping are not all novel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate and end product — two-condition test for unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity between intermediate materials and end products is deemed met where both (①) major structural elements between intermediate materials and end products shall be identical (either same basic chemical structure or technically closely related providing major structural elements), and (②) intermediate materials and end products shall be technically closely related (end products directly produced from intermediates or via few identical intermediates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: 'intermediate' refers to intermediate or starting materials that may lose characteristics and be used to produce end products. Examples: amorphous polymer A (intermediate) and crystalline polymer A (end) produced by orientating film — unity met. High molecular compounds and starting material compounds sharing repeating unit X — unity met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules on multiple intermediate materials and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: One application can be filed on more than one different intermediate material used in different processes to produce a single end material if major structural elements are identical. However, more than two different intermediate materials used in other structures of end products cannot be filed as one application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance limits combining many structurally different intermediates in one application even if they lead to a common end product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation by non-novel intermediate prevents joint filing
rubrics_metrics.description: If intermediate materials and end products are separated by an intermediate material which is not novel, such materials cannot be filed as one patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should check novelty of intermediates in production chain when assessing unity grouping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Groups of compounds correspondence rule (intermediate vs end product groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where intermediate materials and end products are groups of chemical compounds, each intermediate compound shall correspond to one compound claimed in the group of end product compounds; but groups do not necessarily correspond one-to-one if parts of end materials lack corresponding intermediate compounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should analyze one-to-one correspondence between claimed compound groups; lack of correspondence may break unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity determination begins with independent claims; dependents inherit unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention shall be first determined on independent claims. Where independent claims are deemed to meet unity, dependent claims which refer to such independent claims shall be deemed to satisfy unity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a primary procedural principle for examiners. Dependent claims are generally not separately assessed if the independent claim meets unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity as ground for rejection and division suggestion
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement of unity under Article 45 may constitute a ground for rejection under Article 62 of the Patent Act. An examiner may suggest division of an application when notifying a ground for rejection to facilitate applicant response and speed/accuracy of examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although unity can lead to rejection, examiners are encouraged to suggest divisional filings where appropriate to aid applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments can change unity; deletion or content change may break unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if unity is met based on an independent claim at one point, subsequent deletion or amendment of that independent claim can change the content so that the requirement of unity is no longer satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must reassess unity after claim amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generally no need to determine unity between independent and dependent claims, except when cited claim lacks novelty/inventive step
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle, unity does not need to be determined between an independent claim and a dependent claim dependent upon it; however, where a cited claim lacks novelty or inventive step and thus lacks 'special technical features', unity cannot be met among claims citing the concerned claim and additional review is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows independent claim A disclosed in prior art and dependent claims A+B, A+C, A+C+D, A+F: since independent claim lacks improvement, unity must be determined among dependent claims (claims 2-5) and examiner may split into groups (Group1: claims1-2; Group2: claims3-4; Group3: claim5) and notify accordingly. Examiner may also directly notify rejection on grounds of lack of novelty/inventive step for all claims if searching all groups is unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of microorganisms required prior to filing unless easily obtainable by skilled person
rubrics_metrics.description: A person wishing to file a patent application for an invention related to a microorganism shall deposit the microorganism with designated authorities prior to filing, unless a person with ordinary skill in the art can easily obtain the microorganism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows Article 2 of the Enforcement Decree: deposit with either a domestic depository authority designated by the Commissioner of KIPO or an international depository authority under the Budapest Treaty. If not deposited because the microorganism is easily obtainable, the applicant must disclose the method by which the microorganism was acquired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depository authorities and disclosure of deposit number
rubrics_metrics.description: Depositories include domestic authorities designated by KIPO (e.g., KCTC, KCCM, KACC) and international depositories (e.g., KCTC, KCCM, KCLRF). Applicants who have deposited must state the deposit number in the patent application specification and attach documents evidencing the deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If deposit number is given after filing, applicant or patentee shall report it to the Commissioner without delay. For international-phase filings, deposit to an international authority must be before filing date of the patent application and intention must be stated and proving documents enclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of deposit — supplement enablement for biological materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposit supplements the specification to ensure a person with ordinary skill in the art can easily practice the invention when starting materials or end products include biological materials that cannot be fully enabled by disclosure alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should disclose means of obtaining starting materials and manufacturing methods in detail; deposit supports practicability when specification alone is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of biological materials subject to deposit
rubrics_metrics.description: Microorganisms subject to deposit include biological materials such as genes, vectors, germs, mold, animal cells, fertilized eggs, seeds, etc.; types eligible for deposit differ according to each depository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even plant-related inventions may require deposit of parent plants, seeds, or cells where necessary to enable practice by a skilled person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microorganisms that can be 'easily secured' (no deposit required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Microorganisms easily secured under Article 2 include: (i) those currently sold in the market; (ii) those deposited at credible depositories before application filing and confirmed eligible for distribution (with depository/distribution evidence disclosed); (iii) microorganisms that can be easily produced by a person skilled in the art based on the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the microorganism falls into these categories, deposit may not be required, but depository and deposit number should be disclosed where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedure — attach evidential document or describe acquisition method
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant intending to file on an invention related to a microorganism shall deposit the microorganism and attach evidential document on the deposit to the patent application. Where a microorganism is not deposited (because easily obtainable), the applicant shall describe how to obtain the microorganism in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proving documents must be attached; where same documents were submitted for prior related applications, applicant may state intention to refer to submitted documents instead of resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination rules (applications filed before Dec 31, 2014) — missing deposit certificate treated as not deposited
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application includes the fact of deposit and the deposit number but not a copy of the deposit certificate, an examiner shall consider that the microorganism is not deposited and conduct examination on the application. If the applicant later attaches the deposit certificate after notification, the examiner shall accept it and conduct examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amending the original specification to add a deposit number after filing is deemed addition of new matter. If deposit certificate attached before filing, and later the depository changes classification and name, submission of an evidential document copy is acceptable and not deemed new matter unless new scientific characteristics not in original specification are stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit must be completed by the time of filing; date of deposit defined; failure to submit certificate invalidates deposit as of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The deposit shall be completed by the time of filing the application. The time of deposit is the date when applicant deposits the microorganism and the depository receives it. If applicant discloses only the deposit number but fails to submit the deposit certificate through amendment, it shall be deemed that deposit was never made on the date of deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must ensure deposit certificate is submitted in timely fashion; examiners treat incomplete proof as no deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formalities examination rules (applications filed after Jan 1, 2015) — deficiencies and invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: In formalities examination, examiners check whether microorganism stated in proving documents was deposited before filing. If microorganism was not deposited before filing, or name/authority/number/date incorrectly stated, deficiencies shall be communicated and proposed to remedy; failure to remedy within time limit may result in invalidation of the proceeding related to the deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proving documents attached without indicating intention or vice versa, this contravenes rules and amendments shall be proposed; lack of remedy can invalidate deposit proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination for deposit-related applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there are no deficiencies identified in documents submitted by the applicant regarding deposit, substantive examination shall be conducted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is procedural: deposit-related formalities must be cleared before substantive examination continues for microorganism-related inventions.
